---
title: Getting started
---

## Connect from a browser

The library uses `wsconnect` from `@nats-io/nats-core`. Use a `ws://` or `wss://` server URL, not the TCP `nats://` address. An HTTPS page needs a secure `wss://` endpoint.

```ts
import { createActor } from 'xstate'
import { natsMachine } from '@jr200-labs/xstate-nats'

const actor = createActor(natsMachine)
actor.subscribe((snapshot) => console.log(snapshot.value))
actor.start()

actor.send({
  type: 'CONFIGURE',
  config: {
    opts: { servers: ['ws://localhost:42222'], timeout: 3000 },
    maxRetries: 3,
  },
})
actor.send({ type: 'CONNECT' })
```

Wait for `snapshot.matches('connected')` before sending messaging or KV events. The root waits for both child managers to report readiness. A failed initial connection enters `error`; send `CONNECT` again to retry or `CONFIGURE` to replace the configuration.

For React, use the same machine with `useActor(natsMachine)` from `@xstate/react`. The library has no React dependency.

## Run a local NATS broker

Install [nats-server](https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/introduction/installation), then use the repository's development configuration:

```bash
nats-server -c nats-server.conf
```

This enables JetStream and an unencrypted development WebSocket listener on port `42222`. Preview the demo locally and select **Live WebSocket** with `ws://localhost:42222`. The config has verbose development logging; use your own TLS, origin policy, and authentication for a deployed broker. See [NATS WebSocket configuration](https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/websocket/websocket_conf).

## Close and recover

```ts
actor.send({ type: 'DISCONNECT' })
// Wait for closed, then reconnect with the current configuration:
actor.send({ type: 'CONNECT' })
```

`DISCONNECT` drains and closes the connection. `RESET` is available in `configured`, `closed`, and `error`; it clears the root configuration. Send `DISCONNECT` and wait for `closed` before resetting an active session. Calling `actor.stop()` alone is not a replacement for disconnecting the broker connection.

## Build the documentation

Use Node.js 22.12+ and the pnpm version in `package.json`. Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm demo:dev              # browser demo at http://localhost:3001
quarto preview docs        # complete documentation site
quarto render docs         # static output in docs/_site
```

Quarto's pre-render hook installs locked dependencies and builds the demo. Its relative asset paths work both locally and under the GitHub Pages project path. The Documentation workflow renders a preview on pull requests and publishes through the shared Quarto workflow after changes reach `master`.
